posts.title: In Touch, Inworld
posts.description: If you're old enough to remember the early days of opensim, you will remember how hit and miss communications were. There were scores of grids, and no end of wide open spaces, but not a lot of people, and those that were on one grid, often had little or no idea of the existence of other people in other places. Being a bit countercultural, often curmudgeonly, and also busy building, that was fine for most people most of the time. But humans are gregarious at heart. How to stay in touch? IRC, the 80's way of communicating, was favored by many of the geeks behind the opensimulator code and you could wait literally days for someone to answer a question. This Map made by Pathfinder Lester back in the day gives you an idea of our horizons among the hg enabled grids. Between hypergridders, news about events was largely a matter of word of mouth, or habit - like the regular Friday dance on OSGrid run by Dorothea Lundquist and the late and much missed Jay Maze . posts.title: Safari Goes to the End of the Line
posts.description: For our final stop in this season's regular trips, we went for a first time visit to a fairly new grid, Holoneon . Run by Fiona and Niki Sweet, they suggested a great region for us to explore, called Haven City . It's themed around the movie Tron , a classic bit of scifi and just perfect for our group. 'End of the Line' is a movie reference and a track by Daft Punk - the Safari tours will be back in January! (and some Specials before that, too.) On Holoneon, we were lucky enough to have as our guides the builders of the sim, Angel and Jade Madison. HG Address is (and you knew this was coming) at the end of the post, so you remember to go visit! Bit of an unrezzed start to our tour, but as you all know, it takes us a while to get our act together. Luckily, the girls of the grid were pretty patient with us. ~Ąиցєℓ~: Welcome everyone.
